newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 10.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** Indian Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda says his government will soon take significant decisions to improve the climate for foreign investment even if it met with difficulties on the way.
"The economic reform process has generated considerable
enthusiasm and opened up vast sectors of activity," Deve Gowda told an international business conference organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) in Calcutta on Thursday.
"Considerable progress has been achieved but we are
aware of the pending issues at both the national and the state level which need to be addressed. We are determined to move forward even if at times the going gets to be tough."
** Finance Minister P. Chidambaram says his government is ready to cut taxes if there was an increase in the number of taxpayers, and said he saw signs that this could happen.
"If the tax base grows as much as I like and expect it
to grow, you will find in response a reduction in tax rates," Chidambaram told an international business conference in Calcutta.
** Chidambaram told the same meeting he would take a decision on the controversial Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) on corporations soon.
The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Chidambaram as
saying he was aware of industry's opposition to the tax he imposed in last year's budget.
** A government commission studying the possible sale of partial stakes in state-owned companies will submit its first report in February, Indian Finance Minister Chidambaram said.
Last year the government asked the Disinvestment
Commission to study the possibility of selling off partial stakes in 40 state-controlled companies.
"That commission has promised me that the first report
will come in early February," Chidambaram told the Confederation of Indian Industry's annual meeting in Calcutta.
India aims to raise 50 billion rupees in 1996/97
(April-March) by selling off shares in state companies.

** British Prime Minister John Major, currently touring South Asia, urged India on Thursday to open up its insurance sector to foreign competition, cut tariffs on imports of consumer goods and offer protection to intellectual property.
Major told the Confederation of Indian Industry's annual
meeting in Calcutta that three key sectors for further economic progress in India were telecommunications, financial services and consumer goods.
"Opening up the insurance sector, for example, would
also contribute significantly to long-term growth, providing scarce funds for infrastructural development," Major said.
The Indian government has promised to open up its
state-controlled insurance sector to private firms, both domestic and foreign.
** State-run Steel Authority of India Ltd (SAIL) plans to invest 150 billion rupees on modernisation and expansion over the next five years, the government said on Thursday.
SAIL has invested 200 billion rupees in modernisation
and expansion since 1986, it said in a statement.
MARKETS:
** The Indian rupee opened lower at 35.875/885 against the dollar on Friday against the previous close of 35.865/875 and is seen rangebound, dealers said.
** Shares across Indian bourses rallied on Thursday as foreign funds and speculators pressed buy orders in front-line stocks, dealers said.
Market sentiment was pepped up by a number of government
statements on Thursday which marketmen viewed as positive.

** Bombay benchmark index surges 2.24 percent to close at 3,362.39. Delhi index gains 1.18 percent, Calcutta index up 1.31 percent and Madras index advances 2.09 points. National bourse index adds 9.90 points to 956.60.
-- Feizal Samath, Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
